chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Hashim, the master of the post, who said:

I, Muhammad ibn Muslim, and Abu al-Khattab were gathered together. Abu al-Khattab said to us, 'What do you say about one who does not recognize this matter?' I said, 'One who does not recognize this matter is a disbeliever (kafir).' Abu al-Khattab said, 'He is not a disbeliever until the proof (hujjah) is established upon him. When the proof is established upon him and he does not recognize, then he is a disbeliever.' Muhammad ibn Muslim said to him, 'Glory be to Allah! What is his case when he does not recognize and does not deny? Is he not a disbeliever when he does not deny?'

He said, 'So when I performed Hajj, I entered upon Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him of that. He said, 'You have attended and those two are absent, but your appointment is tonight at the Middle Jamrah in Mina.' So when it was the night, we gathered with him, Abu al-Khattab and Muhammad ibn Muslim.

He took a pillow and placed it on his chest, then said to us, 'What do you say about your servants, your women, and your family? Do they not testify that there is no god but Allah?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Do they not testify that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family)?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Do they not pray, fast, and perform Hajj?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Do they recognize what you are upon?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'So what are they in your view?' I said, 'One who does not recognize this matter is a disbeliever.'

He said, 'Glory be to Allah! Do you not see the people of the roads and the people of the waters?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Do they not pray, fast, and perform Hajj? Do they not testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Do they recognize what you are upon?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'So what are they in your view?' I said, 'One who does not recognize this matter is a disbeliever.'

He said, 'Glory be to Allah! Do you not see the Ka'bah, the Tawaf, and the people of Yemen and their clinging to the curtains of the Ka'bah?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Do they not testify that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and do they not pray, fast, and perform Hajj?' I said, 'Yes.' He said, 'Do they recognize what you are upon?' I said, 'No.' He said, 'So what do you say about them?' I said, 'One who does not recognize is a disbelieer.'
He said, 'Glory be to Allah! This is the saying of the Kharijites.'

Then he said, 'If you wish, I will inform you.' I said, 'As for me, no.' He said, 'Indeed, it is an evil upon you if you say something that you have not heard from us.' He said, 'So I guessed that he was turning us toward the saying of Muhammad ibn Muslim.'

key_terms.الطَّوَافَ: Tawaf, the ritual circumambulation of the Ka'bah
key_terms.الْأَمْرَ: The matter, specifically referring to Wilayah (authority) of the Imams in this context
key_terms.الْحُجَّةُ: The proof or evidence established by God, often referring to the Imam or clear divine signs
key_terms.الْخَوَارِجِ: The Kharijites, a early Islamic sect known for declaring other Muslims as disbelieers
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةَ: The Ka'bah, the sacred house in Mecca

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia view on whether a Muslim is a disbelieer if they do not know about the Imams?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia doctrine of 'Tahkim' (acceptance of authority) by contrasting the Kharijite tendency to declare Muslims disbelievers for lacking specific theological knowledge with the Ahl al-Bayt's more nuanced approach. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) uses analogies of servants and pilgrims to demonstrate that while ritual practice and Prophethood are foundational, Wilayah recognition requires established proof (hujjah), preventing premature excommunication (takfir) of those who are simply unaware. This narrative underscores the scholarly principle that ignorance, distinct from denial, does not necessarily constitute disbelief unless the proof has been clearly presented to the individual.
